summary: Summation No. 18 covers March 1947 in South Korea under USAMGIK. Politically it records the Military Governor's pledge of no government reorganization without Korean consent, the Interim Legislative Assembly's first reading of a rightist temporary constitution (11 March) and general franchise law (25 March), the Chungking group's 2 March claim to be the de jure government, and the final report of the Chief U.S. Commissioner on the Moscow Agreement. Public order centred on 1 March Independence Day clashes, Cheju-do strikes and the 22-23 March general strike called by the Chun Pyung Labor Union. Economic sections give coal, steel, textile, paper, banking, trade, rail, communications, ration and price data, including 30 American locomotives, new ration books and 30 percent coal price rises. Social sections cover typhoid, refugees, the Korean Red Cross, student strikes and press opinion. Useful for the transition toward Korean self-government and the strike wave.
highlights: On 12 March the Military Governor announced that no reorganization of the South Korean Interim Government would occur without a majority of the Korean Directorate under Civil Administrator Ahn Chai Hong, or enacted law of the Assembly.

On 11 March Suh Sang Il and 54 rightist legislators presented a draft temporary constitution to the Interim Legislative Assembly; on 25 March Kim Pung Chung introduced a general franchise law giving all citizens over 20 the vote, one representative per 150,000 persons.
On 2 March the former Chungking Provisional Government declared itself the de jure government, naming Syngman Rhee president and Kim Koo vice-president; Military Government declared the act illegal.

A general strike called by the Chun Pyung Labor Union on 22-23 March spread across South Korea, disrupting Seoul transport, printing and utilities; strikes lasted two to three days and disorder was kept minimal.
Thirty American steam locomotives, the first of 100 loaned to the Department of Transportation, reached Pusan on 19 March; imports from Japan included 46,506 tons of coal.
Typhoid cases rose from 659 in February to 1,409 in March, with 580 in Kyongsang-pukto; typhus fell to 208.
Rice collection ended 15 March with 650,646 kiloliters collected; 8,631 people were detained for non-compliance, of whom 6,339 were acquitted. New ration books issued from 16 March.
Korean National Police strength reached 26,386 in January, and the February prison population rose to 17,431; Coast Guard seized 171 vessels in 1946 for illegal commerce.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Covers, title pages for Summation No. 18 (March 1947), table of contents and list of 36 charts, maps and graphs, with the Digitized by Google (University of Virginia) stamps.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Brief digest of the month: the Assembly's draft constitution and franchise law, general strike of 21-23 March, coal price rises, typhoid increase and Red Cross founding.

sections.title: Section 1. Political Activities
sections.summary: Draft constitution by 55 rightists on 11 March, franchise law reported 25 March, Chungking Government's 2 March claim, final Joint Commission report, and Ordinance 118 amendment.

sections.title: Section 2. Economic Activities
sections.summary: Fertilizer need of 330,463 tons, February coal shortfall, 1946 cotton output, 22 March general strike, 30 locomotives from Germany, quadrupled radio fees and new ration books.

sections.title: Section 3. Social Activities
sections.summary: Typhoid up to 1,409 cases, Red Cross charter on 16 March, repatriation figures, Seoul National University registration of 3,396, youth movement membership of 43,994 and radio programs.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Government reorganization policy, Assembly business, strikes and Independence Day, police and prison figures, Constabulary and Coast Guard, and the Joint Commission's final report.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Military Governor's 12 March reorganization pledge, Assembly's summer-grain letter, constitution and franchise law, Democratic Women's League petition, Chungking claim, Joint Commission report, Delhi conference observers.

sections.title: Administration
sections.summary: Military Governor's statement of 12 March that reorganization needs Directorate approval; civil-service examinations began, 300 clerk applicants on 31 March; statistics course from 24 March.

sections.title: Korean Interim Legislative Assembly
sections.summary: Summer-grain collection request due 1 April, first act barring dual office, draft constitution on 11 March, Seoul National University proposals, franchise law of 25 March and Women's League demands.

sections.title: Political Developments
sections.summary: Chungking Government's 2 March declaration with Rhee and Kim Koo, Cheju-do employee strike 11-18 March, and People's Front demand to punish collaborators.

sections.title: U.S.-U.S.S.R. Joint Commission
sections.summary: Fifth and final report of the Chief U.S. Commissioner defending the Moscow Agreement and the word trusteeship, quoting General Hodge's appeal against agitation.

sections.title: Foreign Affairs
sections.summary: Three Korean observers left 17 March for the Pan-Asiatic Conference at Delhi; British Consulate General in Seoul formally recognized 27 March.

sections.title: Section 2. Legal and Public Safety
sections.summary: Ordinances 131 and 133, universal suffrage ordinance request, Independence Day and 22-23 March strikes, police strength of 26,386, prison population of 17,431, Constabulary and Coast Guard.

sections.title: Major Legislation and Legal
sections.summary: Ordinance 131 (6 March) gives Assembly members immunity from arrest; Ordinance 133 (18 March) mandates raw silk inspection; 31 March request for suffrage ordinance if no law by 30 June.

sections.title: Public Safety
sections.summary: Independence Day disorders on Cheju-do with 20,000 at a meeting, strikes of 12 and 22-23 March, police review of 1 March, strength table, 17,431 prisoners and Coast Guard seizures.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: Natural resources, industry, commerce and rationing: coal at 44 percent of requirement, steel doubling, 30 locomotives, Bank of Chosen note decline, new ration books, coal price increases.

sections.title: Section 1. Natural Resources
sections.summary: Agricultural society formed 29 March, 23,894 tons of meat, fat and oil planned, January fish landings of 26,922 tons, December lumber of 1,209,960 board feet, February coal of 21,366 tons.

sections.title: Agriculture
sections.summary: Scientific Agriculture Society meeting, 44 kg of Japanese vegetable seed, Ginseng Growers' Association order revoked, 21 irrigation projects adding 36,368 chungbo.

sections.title: Fisheries
sections.summary: January landings fell to 26,922 tons, 378 tons of bamboo arrived at Pusan on 25 March, and the fishing fleet totals 38,742 vessels.

sections.title: Forestry
sections.summary: December lumber fell 199,920 board feet from November, 15,000 seedlings for Planting Week from 5 April, fuelwood shipment hampered by poor roads.

sections.title: Mining
sections.summary: February coal of 21,366 tons missed quota by 10,834; coal supplied 43.83 percent of need; Hwasun mine produced 5,022 tons; Han Il graphite and Moon Kyung iron mines transferred 1 April.

sections.title: Section 2. Industry
sections.summary: Steel output doubled, paper fell to 282,914 pounds, 1946 cotton yarn of 8,740,400 pounds, 22 March strike, December idle factories 163 of 863 and 47,326 employees.

sections.title: Heavy Industries and Manufacturing
sections.summary: Engineering tests from 17 March, flour at 87,513 bags, canned goods only 219 cases, paper collapse, first American light bulbs 16 March, leather, farm tools and metric system adoption.

sections.title: Textiles
sections.summary: Cotton mills made 8,740,400 pounds of yarn and about 21.7 million yards of cloth in 1946; Ordinance 133 silk testing; 11,031 employed in nine mills.

sections.title: Labor
sections.summary: Chun Pyung strike of 22 March with demands, railway yardmen strike 21 March, WFTU delegation arrival 30 March, employment tables, falling wages and irrigation deadline of 30 June.

sections.title: Section 3. Commerce
sections.summary: Bank of Chosen notes of 17.19 billion yen, gold at 2,500 yen per momme, property custodians' conference, imports from Japan, 30 locomotives, rail rates, mail, telephone and radio statistics.

sections.title: Finance
sections.summary: Notes outstanding fell to 17,191,319,554 on 29 March, Industrial Bank led deposits, gold dropped to 2,500 yen, and tax delinquency was unparalleled.

sections.title: Property Control
sections.summary: Provincial custodians met 20-21 March where the Military Governor spoke of Koreanizing government; machinery returned from Japan; patent applications due 14 April.

sections.title: Imports and Exports
sections.summary: Table of February and March imports from Japan including 46,506 tons of coal and 236 trucks; 30 steam locomotives from Germany; 285 tons of canned food from the United States.

sections.title: Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: Thirty locomotives arrived at Pusan 19 March, rail passenger and freight rates, motor rates from 1 March, eight wooden ships for sale, 117 million kWh delivered in February.

sections.title: Communications
sections.summary: Mail volumes, postal savings and insurance, 141,776 telephone calls, radio fee raised from 10 to 40 yen from 1 May, new 50-kilowatt Seoul transmitter, 18,602 employees.

sections.title: Section 4. Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Cost-of-living differential raised to 1,512 yen in big cities, rice collection total 650,646 kiloliters, new ration books from 16 March, coal price increases, petroleum figures and 8,631 detained.

sections.title: Cost of Living
sections.summary: Government employee differentials of 1,512 to 1,058 yen by locality, steady rise in free-market food prices (rice 1,981.5 yen per bushel) and ceiling prices.

sections.title: Food
sections.summary: Rice collection ended 15 March at 650,646 kiloliters, 8,000 tons of imported barley allocated, new per-person ration books costing 2 yen, seed potato price 32 yen per kwan.

sections.title: Other Goods
sections.summary: Coal dealer prices raised 1 April (anthracite lump 900 to 1,200 yen), pitch to 2,500 yen, 33,000 tons coal allocated, 1946 petroleum distribution totals.

sections.title: Violations
sections.summary: 8,631 detained over rice collection (6,339 acquitted, 367 imprisoned, 1,907 fined); five ships seized for smuggling 1-15 January.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Health and welfare, education and culture, and public information: typhoid surge, Red Cross inauguration, student strikes, youth movement, Radio JODK programs and press reaction to events.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Typhoid 1,409 cases, cholera program from 1 April, rinderpest zone completed, refugee feeding ended 10 March, Red Cross charter 16 March, 392 Koreans repatriated and 4,299 Japanese evacuated.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Culture and Religion
sections.summary: 3,396 students at Seoul National University, Suwon and Pusan school strikes, normal-school principals' conference, youth movement of 43,994, Seoul YMCA joining the international body.

sections.title: Section 3. Public Information
sections.summary: Health films and booklets, Secretary of State's democracy statement broadcast on JODK 21 March, new radio programs, licensing moved to Public Information, and press coverage of 1 March and the strike.

sections.title: Map of Korea
sections.summary: Full-page map of Korea listed at printed page 71, closing the report.
